 // rows of Lk providing the \"B\" operand\n\n    double* __restrict__ C = panels + (size_t)l * Np * NB;\n\n    __shared__ double As[KC][TM];\n    __shared__ double Bs[KC][TN];\n\n    const int tid = threadIdx.x;\n    const int tx = tid % 16;\n    const int ty = tid / 16;\n    const int lr = tid / 4;        // 0..63 load row\n    const int lk = (tid % 4) * 4;  // 0,4,8,12 load k\n\n    double acc[4][4];\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int a = 0; a < 4; ++a)\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) acc[a][b] = 0.0;\n\n    for (int k0 = 0; k0 < kw; k0 += KC) {\n        const double2* pa = reinterpret_cast<const double2*>(Lk + (size_t)(row0 + lr) * NB + k0 + lk);\n        const double2* pb = reinterpret_cast<const double2*>(Lk + (size_t)(brow0 + lr) * NB + k0 + lk);\n        double2 a0 = pa[0], a1 = pa[1];\n        double2 b0 = pb[0], b1 = pb[1];\n        __syncthreads();\n        As[lk + 0][lr] = a0.x; As[lk + 1][lr] = a0.y;\n        As[lk + 2][lr] = a1.x; As[lk + 3][lr] = a1.y;\n        Bs[lk + 0][lr] = b0.x; Bs[lk + 1][lr] = b0.y;\n        Bs[lk + 2][lr] = b1.x; Bs[lk + 3][lr] = b1.y;\n        __syncthreads();\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int kk = 0; kk < KC; ++kk) {\n            double av[4], bv[4];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int a = 0; a < 4; ++a) av[a] = As[kk][ty + 16 * a];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) bv[b] = Bs[kk][tx + 16 * b];\n#pragma unroll\n            for (int a = 0; b < 4; ++b) crow[tx + 16 * b] -= acc[a][b];\n    }\n}\n\n// Factor one panel on the CPU. Returns -1 on success or the global index of the failing diagonal.\nstatic long factorPanelCPU(double* H, size_t m, int w, size_t r0) {\n    // Diagonal block: unblocked Cholesky (same formulation as the reference)\n    for (int i = 0; i < w; ++i) {\n        for (int j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            if (i == j) {\n                for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) sum += H[j * NB + k] * H[j * NB + k];\n                const double val = H[j * NB + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) return (long)(r0 + j);\n                H[j * NB + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) sum += H[i * NB + k] * H[j * NB + k];\n                H[i * NB + j] = (H[i * NB + j] - sum) / H[j * NB + j];\n            }\n        }\n        for (int j = i + 1; j < NB; ++j) H[i * NB + j] = 0.0;\n    }\n    // Rows below the diagonal block: triangular solve, rows are independent\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = w; i < m; ++i) {\n        double* row = H + i * NB;\n        for (int j = 0; j < w; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            const double* lj = H + (size_t)j * NB;\n            for (int k = 0; k < j; ++k) sum += row[k] * lj[k];\n            row[j] = (row[j] - sum) / lj[j];\n        }\n    }\n    return -1;\n}\n\n// Distributed state prepared before the timed section\nstruct DistMatrix {\n    size_t n = 0;\n    int NT = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        const double* src = H + (i - r0) * NB;\n        double* dst = &A[i * n + r0];\n        for (int c = 0; c < w; ++c) dst[c] = src[c];\n        if (i < r0 + w) {\n            // last panel touching row i: zero out upper triangular part\n            for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, DistMatrix& D) {\n    const size_t n = D.n;\n    const int NT = D.NT;\n    const size_t Np = D.Np;\n    const size_t panelElems = Np * NB;\n    if (NT == 0) return true;\n\n    double* dPanels = nullptr;\n    double* dL = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dPanels, std::max<size_t>(1, D.nloc * panelElems) * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dL, panelElems * sizeof(double)));\n    double* hbuf[2];\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMallocHost(&hbuf[0], (panelElems + 1) * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMallocHost(&hbuf[1], (panelElems + 1) * sizeof(double)));\n\n    cudaStream_t sMain, sLook;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&sMain, cudaStreamNonBlocking));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&sLook, cudaStreamNonBlocking));\n    cudaEvent_t evL;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventCreateWithFlags(&evL, cudaEventDisableTiming));\n\n    if (D.nloc > 0)\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(dPanels, D.hLocal, D.nloc * panelElems * sizeof(double),\n                                   cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, sMain));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(sMain));\n\n    auto devPanel = [&](int j) { return dPanels + (size_t)(j / g_size) * panelElems; };\n\n    // Factor panel j (owned locally, device copy up to date) on CPU; result into hbuf and device\n    auto factorOwned = [&](int j, double* hb, cudaStream_t s) {\n        const size_t r0 = (size_t)j * NB;\n        const size_t m = Np - r0;\n        double* dp = devPanel(j) + r0 * NB;\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(hb, dp, m * NB * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, s));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(s));\n        const size_t mValid = n - r0;\n        const int w = (int)std::min<size_t>(NB, n - r0);\n        const long st = factorPanelCPU(hb, mValid, w, r0);\n        hb[m * NB] = (double)st;\n        if (st < 0) CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(dp, hb, m * NB * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, s));\n    };\n    auto bcastPanel = [&](int j, double* hb) {\n        const size_t m = Np - (size_t)j * NB;\n        MPI_Bcast(hb + 0, (int)(m * NB + 1), MPI_DOUBLE, ownerOf(j), MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    };\n\n    if (ownerOf(0) == g_rank) factorOwned(0, hbuf[0], sLook);\n    // status sits right after the panel data; 4x4 register blocks\n// provide independent accumulation chains.\nstatic void symmetricProduct(const double* X, double* out, size_t n, bool lowerTriangularX) {\n    const size_t nb4 = (n + 3) / 4;\n#pragma omp parallel for schedule(dynamic, 1)\n    for (size_t bi = 0; bi < nb4; ++bi) {\n        const size_t i0 = bi * 4;\n        const size_t ni = std::min<size_t>(4, n - i0);\n        for (size_t j0 = 0; j0 <= i0; j0 += 4) {\n            const size_t nj = std::min<size_t>(4, n - j0);\n            double acc[4][4] = {};\n            size_t kmax = n;\n            if (lowerTriangularX) kmax = std::min(n, j0 + nj);  // L[j][k] == 0 for k > j\n            const double* xi[4];\n            const double* xj[4];\n            for (size_t a = 0; a < 4; ++a) xi[a] = X + std::min(i0 + a, n - 1) * n;\n            for (size_t b = 0; b < 4; ++b) xj[b] = X + std::min(j0 + b, n - 1) * n;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < kmax; ++k) {\n                for (int a = 0; a < 4; ++a)\n                    for (int b = 0; b < 4; ++b) acc[a][b] += xi[a][k] * xj[b][k];\n            }\n            for (size_t a = 0; a < ni; ++a)\n                for (size_t b = 0; b < nj; ++b) {\n                    out[(i0 + a) * n + j0 + b] = acc[a][b];\n                    out[(j0 + b) * n + i0 + a] = acc[a][b];\n                }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n\n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n\n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Simple Cholesky decomposition (sequential, unblocked algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            \n            if (i == j) {\n                // Diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                // Off-diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n    \n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    \n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n    \n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n    \n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n    \n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return 0;\n}\n","userModified":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfhkNhuEvG9CvKzAVSLkS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The cholesky benchmark now always runs as MPI + OpenMP + CUDA, and it's much faster: at n=4096 the original takes 17.9 s and the new version takes 58 ms on one GPU. Only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt` changed; no new files and no new dependencies (no cuBLAS or cuSOLVER, the GPU kernels are hand-written). The executable is still `cholesky`.\n\nValidation (`-v`) passes for n = 1, 7, 127, 129, 512, 1000, 1300, 2000, 4096 and 8192, with 1–4 ranks. The output doesn't depend on the rank count, and the printed `Sum` matches the original to all 17 digits in almost every case. The `Hash` line does differ from the original's: the blocked algorithm adds things up in a different order, so results can't be bit-identical. The error is tiny (relative error 1e-11 to 4e-8 against the 1e-6 tolerance). If your checking relies on an exact hash match, it will fail.\n\n**How it works**\n- **MPI:** the matrix is split into 128-column panels dealt round-robin to the ranks, one GPU per rank. Each finished panel is passed around the ranks in a ring, in 512-row chunks so sending and copying overlap. I replaced `MPI_Bcast` because Open MPI's version only reached about 1 GB/s on this machine.\n- **CUDA:** a custom double-precision kernel does the bulk of the work (updating the rest of the matrix) and runs close to the RTX 3090's double-precision peak. A higher-priority stream lets the next panel be computed while that update runs.\n- **OpenMP:** the CPU factors each panel with vectorized loops. This region is limited to 16 threads, because more threads made it slower.\n- **Behaviour kept from the original:** same command-line options and output, same error message and index for a matrix that isn't positive definite (tested), same exit codes. Only rank 0 prints. The input matrix is bit-identical to the original's.\n\n**Timings** (one node, 4× RTX 3090)\n\n| n | 1 GPU | 2 GPUs | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 8192 | ~350 ms | ~230 ms | ~225–250 ms |\n| 16384 | 2560 ms | 1330 ms | ~880 ms |\n\n- **Scaling depends on size.** Two GPUs scale almost perfectly at n=16384; four reach about 2.9x. At n=8192 and below, more ranks barely help (and at n=4096, 2–4 ranks are slightly slower than one). The time there goes on passing panels between ranks, not on computation.\n- **What the timer covers:** copying each rank's share of the matrix to its GPU, the factorization, and gathering the result on rank 0. Matrix generation and the initial hand-out of panels to ranks happen before the timer starts, like generation in the original.\n\n**Changes outside the timed part you should know about**\n- Matrix generation and the `-v` check now run on the GPU. Otherwise, under `mpirun`'s default one-core-per-rank binding, generating the matrix would take minutes. The generation kernel uses the same arithmetic order as the original, which is why the input stays bit-identical.\n- If `mpirun` hasn't already bound a rank to specific CPUs, the program pins it to the CPUs closest to its GPU. This removed large run-to-run variance (np=2 went from 393–523 ms to a steady ~230 ms). If the launcher binds ranks itself, its binding is left alone.\n- If `OMP_NUM_THREADS` isn't set, each rank uses its share of the node's cores.\n\nBuild with `cmake -S cholesky -B build && cmake --build build`, run with e.g. `mpirun -np 4 ./build/cholesky -n 16384 -v`. The GPU architecture is detected automatically unless you set `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":429,"cache_read_input_tokens":123882,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":429},"output_tokens":6,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"4fb4e7f0-93ba-4dd3-bc0f-b9888dec9955","uuid":"dea3e936-97c0-4983-b698-3b6e9d179a90","timestamp":"2026-10-04T19:28:17.388Z","request_id":"req_011CfhkNhaA4cjhZdxeVK3Ps"}

I replaced `MPI_Bcast` because Open MPI's version only reached about 1 GB/s on this machine.\n- **CUDA:** a custom double-precision kernel does the bulk of the work (updating the rest of the matrix) and runs close to the RTX 3090's double-precision peak. A higher-priority stream lets the next panel be computed while that update runs.\n- **OpenMP:** the CPU factors each panel with vectorized loops. This region is limited to 16 threads, because more threads made it slower.\n- **Behaviour kept from the original:** same command-line options and output, same error message and index for a matrix that isn't positive definite (tested), same exit codes. Only rank 0 prints. The input matrix is bit-identical to the original's.\n\n**Timings** (one node, 4× RTX 3090)\n\n| n | 1 GPU | 2 GPUs | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 8192 | ~350 ms | ~230 ms | ~225–250 ms |\n| 16384 | 2560 ms | 1330 ms | ~880 ms |\n\n- **Scaling depends on size.** Two GPUs scale almost perfectly at n=16384; four reach about 2.9x. At n=8192 and below, more ranks barely help (and at n=4096, 2–4 ranks are slightly slower than one). The time there goes on passing panels between ranks, not on computation.\n- **What the timer covers:** copying each rank's share of the matrix to its GPU, the factorization, and gathering the result on rank 0. Matrix generation and the initial hand-out of panels to ranks happen before the timer starts, like generation in the original.\n\n**Changes outside the timed part you should know about**\n- Matrix generation and the `-v` check now run on the GPU. Otherwise, under `mpirun`'s default one-core-per-rank binding, generating the matrix would take minutes. The generation kernel uses the same arithmetic order as the original, which is why the input stays bit-identical.\n- If `mpirun` hasn't already bound a rank to specific CPUs, the program pins it to the CPUs closest to its GPU. This removed large run-to-run variance (np=2 went from 393–523 ms to a steady ~230 ms). If the launcher binds ranks itself, its binding is left alone.\n- If `OMP_NUM_THREADS` isn't set, each rank uses its share of the node's cores.\n\nBuild with `cmake -S cholesky -B build && cmake --build build`, run with e.g. `mpirun -np 4 ./build/cholesky -n 16384 -v`.
